key_insight: Fiber interlayers reshape explosively welded aluminum–steel interfaces and improve penetration resistance through fiber deformation, fracture, and stress-wave regulation.
engineering_relevance: Fiber-reinforced LY12/304L laminates offer a route to lightweight protective structures, provided welding-induced interfacial defects are controlled.
method: Fabricated fiber-reinforced LY12 aluminum/304L steel composites by explosive welding.
Characterized welded interfaces and impact damage using optical and scanning electron microscopy.
Modeled welding with S-ALE and penetration with Lagrangian finite elements.
evidence_signal: The study reports an 11.53% increase in ballistic limit velocity and a 9.9%–49.5% decrease in projectile residual velocity, alongside local stirring velocities of about 2600 m/s near fiber blockage zones.
watch_item: Fiber-induced vortices can initiate interfacial defects; the abstract does not specify fiber architecture or ballistic test conditions needed to assess transferability.
paper_title: Interface formation and anti-penetration mechanism of fiber-reinforced aluminum-steel composites prepared by explosive welding
